CodeLima 1.0.0 makes the Lima VM manager the primary interface. This is a major
release with a new fleet-oriented workflow and substantial daemon changes.

- Manage nodes through global and project-scoped fleet views, live resource
  observations, filtering, grouping, and reviewed batch actions.
- Inspect Overview, Metrics, Logs, and Spec; create and edit reusable templates
  and environment bundles, with disposable environment tests.
- Follow daemon-owned create, start, stop, restart, clone, and delete operations
  in retained Activity history, including failures and cancellation.
- Inspect discovered HTTP/WebSocket routes and explicit TCP mappings in Ports,
  pin shared HTTP ports, and diagnose conflicts and readiness.
- Use direct shell attachment by default, with external window, tmux, and
  opt-in embedded modes. Detach with Ctrl+] while leaving the session running.
- Configure contextual shortcuts, shell launch preferences, and colors. Use
  System for host capacity, doctor checks, daemon controls, and diagnostics.

Upgrade with:

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade codelima
codelima daemon update
codelima --version
```

Reopen the TUI after upgrading. For a fresh Homebrew installation, use
`brew install brianrackle/codelima/codelima`. Lima 2.1.0 or a compatible newer
Lima 2.x release must be on PATH. Linux requires QEMU and KVM access.

Manual archives contain both `codelima` and `codelima-renderer-worker`; keep
them together. Supported targets are macOS arm64, Linux amd64, and Linux arm64.
Publication requires verification, race, CLI integration, and package tests on
all three native targets.

**Known limits:** session kinds distinguish guest and host shells, without
Codex/Claude classification; historical last-up time is not recorded. Final
native visual/input qualification, Linux nested KVM setup, and remaining
startup/handoff edge cases are tracked in
[TODO.md](https://github.com/brianrackle/codelima/blob/v1.0.0/TODO.md).
Existing automated and Linux live checks do not close those manual QA items.
